name: Wave
about: Wave is a 2010s microgenre of melodic, cinematic bass music: slow trap drums around 70 to 80 BPM under washed-out synth pads, pitched vocal fragments, long reverb tails and a melancholy that owes as much to ambient as to rap. It coalesced on SoundCloud around 2014 to 2016, with London producers Klimeks, Kareful, Skit and Vacant at the core, Plastician's Terrorhythm label and its Wavepool compilations giving it a flag, and Kareful's Liquid Ritual a home. The roots are Clams Casino's cloud rap instrumentals, the WeDidIt crew's hazy Los Angeles trap, witch house's drowned textures and the icy production around Yung Lean and Drain Gang. A harder, darker offshoot, hardwave, followed around 2018 with Skeler, Deadcrow and Øfdream. It remains small, mostly instrumental and almost entirely online.

artists.name: Klimeks
artists.why: the sound's first and most melodic voice

artists.name: Kareful
artists.why: Liquid Ritual founder, the scene's organiser

artists.name: Skit
artists.why: early London architect of the style

artists.name: Plastician
artists.why: grime veteran who gave wave its label

artists.name: Sorsari
artists.why: Finnish producer of its darkest textures

albums.title: King Night
albums.why: Witch house's one real album, chopped-and-screwed drums under cathedral synths; wave inherited its drowned, slowed atmosphere wholesale.

albums.title: Instrumentals
albums.why: The cloud rap beats behind Lil B and A$AP Rocky, released on their own: blurred samples, slow drums and reverb as the root of everything wave does.

albums.title: Bad Vibes
albums.why: WeDidIt's founder makes a lo-fi, guitar-flecked beat record of real sadness; the Los Angeles source for wave's hazy drums and mood.

albums.title: Held
albums.why: Tri Angle's masked producer slows garage and R&B fragments to a crawl; the pitched, submerged vocal that became a wave signature starts here.

albums.title: Kings and Them
albums.why: A short Tri Angle set of trap drums and cold, ringing synths that showed how rap production could be turned into atmosphere.

albums.title: Unknown Memory
albums.why: Yung Gud, Yung Sherman and Whitearmor's glacial production under Lean's drowsy rap; the Sad Boys aesthetic wave's producers absorbed.

albums.title: Dark Red
albums.why: Heavier and more cinematic than the debut, with distorted drums and horror-film synths; the closest thing to a wave template before the term existed.

albums.title: Plastician Presents: Wavepool
albums.why: Terrorhythm's compilation that named and gathered the scene, Klimeks, Kareful, Skit and friends in one place for the first time; a document more than a classic.

albums.title: Plastician Presents: Wavepool 2
albums.why: The sequel caught wave at its peak reach, deeper and better sequenced than the first, with the melodic and hard wings both represented.

albums.title: Icedancer
albums.why: Whitearmor's crystalline, weightless beats under Bladee's processed voice; Drain Gang and wave share this exact palette of pads and pitched vocals.

albums.title: E
albums.why: Short, airy and strange, with trap drums dissolving into ambient pop; the record wave's melodic producers most often point to from the era.

note: Wave's own releases are mostly singles and EPs on SoundCloud and Bandcamp; this list is the two compilations that define it and the records its producers built on.
